title: Al-Mu'akhkhir, the Delayer
hook: the Delayer, who puts back in wisdom
tomorrow: before the first word of anything, what do Muslims say?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Muqaddim, the one who brings forward, and a hand on a shoulder: don't wait for morning. The line: brought forward. Today, the other half of that same prayer.

Delayed in transit. A new departure time in orange letters on the board. Delivered, not read. Yesterday's question was what happens when He puts something back, and today's Name is exactly that: Al-Mu'akhkhir, the Delayer, the one who puts back. It's a hard Name to love on a waiting day. So one question for today: is a delay a no?
screen: `DELAYED IN TRANSIT.` → `THE ONE WHO PUTS BACK.` → `IS A DELAY A NO?`

segments.voice: Islam's answer starts with the pair. In the Prophet's du'a, the two Names stand together: the one who brings forward, the one who puts back. Same hand, same wisdom. The Qur'an says it plainly, in Pickthall's words: "it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you," and it ends, "Allah knoweth, ye know not." And in Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says a person's du'a is answered as long as they don't grow impatient and say, I prayed, and nothing came. So in this picture, put back is not thrown out. Now a neighbor says something close. In the Bible, Ecclesiastes, read by Jews and Christians alike, opens a famous chapter: "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven." A time to plant, it goes on, and a time to pluck up. What's shared is real: time isn't ours to run, and things have their hour. And here's the honest difference, ranking no one. Ecclesiastes lists the seasons, and keeps admitting that no one can find out God's work from beginning to end. Islam takes the delay itself and gives it a Name of God, one you can call on in a du'a, ya Mu'akhkhir. One names the seasons. The other names the One who sets them.
screen: `THE PAIR: FORWARD AND BACK.` · `YE HATE A THING WHICH IS GOOD.` · `A NEIGHBOR: A TIME FOR EVERY PURPOSE.` · `ONE NAMES THE SEASONS, ONE THE SETTER.` · then, large: `PUT BACK.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and name one thing that's on hold: a reply, a result, a healing. Don't push it forward and don't throw it away. For the sit, just set it down on a shelf in your mind, put back, not lost.
screen: `ONE THING ON HOLD.` · `ON THE SHELF, NOT IN THE TRASH.`

segments.voice: Al-Mu'akhkhir. The Delayer: the one who puts back in wisdom, named right beside the one who brings forward.
Carry this: put back, on a shelf you can't see from here. Name seventy-two, and the week nearly done.
